name: Dispatch Guard
description: Middleware that enforces an orchestrator agent's output routing at the tool seam: denies deliverable-shaped writes (deliverable dirs/extensions, outside the whitelist) with a dispatch hint, warns on shell commands producing deliverables, and backstops a disabled spawn_subagent. Reads and basic file operations are never intercepted.

description_i18n.zh-CN: 在工具接缝层强制编排 agent 的产出路由：交付物形状的写入（交付物目录/扩展名，白名单外）直接拒绝并提示派发给对应 agent，shell 交付物启发式仅警告，spawn_subagent 兜底拦截。读操作与基础文件读写永不拦截。
description_i18n.en-US: Enforces an orchestrator agent's output routing at the tool seam: deny deliverable-shaped writes outside the whitelist, warn-only shell heuristics, spawn backstop. Reads and basic file operations are never intercepted.

author: leo

meta.notes: No agent-facing tools. The plugin ships routes.example.json (a sanitized sample table); you write your own routes.json: in the plugin directory (explicit override, checked first) or in <host>/plugin-data/dispatch-guard/ (durable home that survives plugin reinstalls — the installer rebuilds the plugin directory on every install; the plugin mirrors the plugin-dir copy there after every reload). mode (enforce|warn|off, hot-reloaded by mtime), deliverable_dirs / deliverable_exts (what counts as a deliverable — they extend the built-in defaults), shell_enforce (opt-in deny of shell commands producing deliverables, closes the redirect/copy bypass), write_tools (extra write-capable tool names; paths inside their arguments are scanned), routes (keyword -> agent), ext_routes (extension -> agent). Two coverage tiers: explicit write targets (redirect/tee/-o/--outdir/cp destination/ffmpeg positional output) follow the full write rules and can be denied; quoted mentions only warn. Tables are linted and type-normalized at load (contradictions, dead rules, unknown modes; a wrong-typed field degrades to absent instead of crashing). Only deliverable-shaped, non-whitelisted writes whose owner actually exists here are guarded: specialist agents are discovered from agents/*/agent.json manifests, a route naming an absent agent passes with a no_owner audit record (no owner, no block). A fresh install drafts routes.draft.json (mode=warn, in the plugin-data dir, adopted not regenerated) from the discovered agents' declared dispatch policy — review it and rename to routes.json to activate; routes.json and routes.draft.json are private, gitignored, never packaged. Reads and basic writes (notes, scripts, configs, scratch) pass untouched in every mode. Interception log: <workspace>/logs/dispatch_guard.jsonl (summarize with packaging/audit_summary.py). Design grounding: docs/RESEARCH.md
